This is an optional, non‑critical scene that follows the player's rescue of a frightened street child, Mirkon, from harpies — either immediately after the waterside fight or later in the Den hideout where the kids shelter. Mirkon is a terrified, snivelling tiefling boy (cowering, hands over his face/ears) who, unless the player already snapped him out of it, is still enchanted by a harpy's song and compelled to move closer to it. The player is acting as rescuer/guardian and will speak bluntly or brusquely to steady him and warn that the harpies and their lure could return. Nearby kids (led by Mol) or any companions present can change the tone or available responses, but the scene primarily illustrates Mirkon’s trauma rather than advancing main-story beats.

Just before this exchange the player fought off a pair of harpies that had enchanted a small tiefling child and tried to eat him; the player has already pulled the child out of immediate danger. The child, Mirkon, is still terrified and physically cowering (hands over his face/ears), barely able to answer and prone to snivelling. The player is in the role of rescuer/guardian here, speaking bluntly and a bit brusquely to steady the child and warn that the harpies could return. This is an optional, non‑critical scene meant to show the child's trauma and the immediate aftermath rather than advance main‑story beats.

After a mind meld (vision where he sees a glimpse of your past) you can convince him that you're both victims and should work together to find an answer. Once he realises you're not a threat his tone changes from threatening to charming.
